# C4 Model

Birnio's architecture in C4 levels. Birnio is a local-first desktop app; the only
external system is the remote API the user queries.

## Level 1 — Context

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    user([Developer/QA])
    birnio[Birnio<br/>GTK desktop API client]
    api[(Remote HTTP APIs)]
    files[(Collection files<br/>Postman/Bruno/Insomnia)]

    user -->|edits and sends requests| birnio
    birnio -->|HTTP/HTTPS| api
    files -->|imports| birnio
```

## Level 2 — Containers (crates)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph app[Birnio workspace]
        ui[birnio-ui-gtk<br/>GTK4/libadwaita/Relm4 · binary]
        core[birnio-core<br/>domain model]
        http[birnio-http<br/>execution via reqwest]
        storage[birnio-storage<br/>persistence sqlx/SQLite]
        import[birnio-import<br/>format adapters]
    end
    api[(Remote APIs)]

    ui --> core
    ui --> http
    ui --> storage
    ui --> import
    http --> core
    storage --> core
    import --> core
    http -->|reqwest| api
```

`birnio-core` is the stable center with no internal dependencies. `http`,
`storage`, and `import` depend only on `core`. `ui-gtk` orchestrates them all.

## Level 3 — Components of birnio-ui-gtk

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph ui[birnio-ui-gtk]
        shell[shell/<br/>window, header, sidebar, navigation]
        services[services/<br/>app_context, command]
        subgraph features[features/]
            re[request_editor]
            rv[response_viewer]
            col[collections]
            env[environments]
            set[settings]
        end
    end
    http[birnio-http]
    storage[birnio-storage]

    shell --> features
    features --> services
    services --> http
    services --> storage
```

Each feature follows the `component / message / state / mod` quartet (TEA style).
Business logic stays in the library crates; `services/` is the bridge.

## Level 4 — Code (critical component: HttpExecutor)

The most critical flow is request execution in `birnio-http`:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    req[&Request domain] --> build[request_builder::build]
    build --> rq[reqwest::Request]
    rq --> exec[client.execute]
    exec --> resp[reqwest::Response]
    resp --> parse[response_parser::parse]
    parse --> out[Response domain + elapsed]
```

The `HttpExecutor` trait uses RPIT `+ Send` (not `async fn`) to keep the future
`Send` — see the comment in `executor.rs` and [MADR.md](MADR.md) ADR-0005.
